identity_anchors: cyan and magenta chromatic aberration (glitch) offset effect
white core shape with colored edge shifts
must_preserve: The specific geometry of the 'd' note shape (vertical stem, top right flag, bottom left loop)
The tri-color layering relationship (white center, cyan shift, magenta shift)
The direction of the color offsets (cyan to top-left, magenta to bottom-right)
The negative space inside the bottom loop
can_restyle: Background texture or gradient (as long as it remains dark/high contrast)
Icon container shape (squircle vs circle vs rounded square)
Intensity of the glow or shadow effects
Exact hue saturation of the cyan/magenta (can be softened but not removed)
must_not_replace_with: Generic musical notes without the specific 'd' shape
Standard flat icons without the glitch/offset effect
color_preservation: The cyan (#25F4EE approx) and magenta/red (#FE2C55 approx) are critical identity colors. They must remain distinct from the white core. The dark background is essential for the neon/glitch effect to work; light backgrounds will destroy the identity. Colors can be slightly desaturated for soft themes but cannot be changed to arbitrary palettes (e.g., all blue or all green).
structure_summary: A white stylized lowercase 'd' resembling a musical note, featuring a signature chromatic aberration effect where a cyan layer shifts top-left and a magenta layer shifts bottom-right, set against a solid dark background.
risk_notes: Removing the cyan/magenta offset makes it look like a generic music app.
Changing the background to white/light gray ruins the neon aesthetic.
Altering the 'd' shape proportions breaks brand recognition.
Over-stylizing the edges (e.g., making them too fuzzy or hand-drawn) loses the digital/tech feel.
